Directions: Based on the passages below and on your knowledge of social studies, answer each question that follows.
Content: ... The influence of laissez faire on the treatment of Ireland during the famine is impossible to exaggerate. Almost without exception the high officials and politicians responsible for Ireland were fervent [strong] believers in non-interference by Government, and the behaviour of the British authorities only becomes explicable [understandable] when their fanatical belief in private enterprise and their suspicions of any action which might be considered Government intervention are borne in mind. ...
